title: PMP vs PRINCE2: Which Certification Should You Get?
dek: Get the PMP if you want a globally recognized, versatile credential (strongest in the US, Asia and the Middle East); get PRINCE2 if you work in the UK, Europe or government, where its methodology is the standard. Many professionals eventually hold both.

seo.metaDescription: PMP vs PRINCE2 compared on approach, region, cost, and structure — plus why they're not really rivals and when to get each (or both).

sources.label: PeopleCert — PRINCE2 (owner of the PRINCE2 certification)

body.richText: PMP and PRINCE2 are the two most recognized project management credentials in the world, but they're not really the same kind of thing — and where you live matters as much as which you choose. One is a global profession-based certification; the other is a certification in a specific methodology.

Quick answer: in the US, Asia or the Middle East, the PMP is usually the safer bet. In the UK, Europe, Australia or government-heavy sectors, PRINCE2 is often expected. Check the job postings in your market before you choose.

The PMP, from the Project Management Institute (PMI), certifies you as a professional across the whole discipline — it's knowledge-based, drawn from PMI's body of knowledge, and it applies to any methodology or industry. PRINCE2, owned by PeopleCert, certifies that you understand and can apply a specific process-based methodology for project governance and control. In short: PMP says "this person is a capable project manager"; PRINCE2 says "this person knows the PRINCE2 method."

body.richText: A cost note on PRINCE2: since 2024, PeopleCert bundles a mandatory official digital manual with each exam voucher, and prices vary a lot by country and whether you buy training. Always confirm the current price on PeopleCert's site for your region.

body.richText: Don't pick based on prestige alone — pick on geography and employer demand. A PMP carries less weight in a PRINCE2-standard government office, and PRINCE2 is less recognized in a US tech company. The job market you're entering decides this more than the certifications' reputations do.

Yes — and plenty of experienced project managers do, because they're complementary rather than competing. PRINCE2 gives you a structured method; the PMP gives you broad professional recognition. If you're early-career, though, don't do both at once — start with whichever fits your market, build experience, and add the other later if it helps.

items.question: Is PMP or PRINCE2 better?
items.answerRichText: Neither is universally better — it depends on where you work. The PMP is the global standard and dominates the US, Asia and the Middle East; PRINCE2 is expected across the UK, Europe, Australia and government. Match the certification to your job market.

items.question: Is PRINCE2 recognized in the US?
items.answerRichText: Less than the PMP. PRINCE2 is well recognized in the UK, Europe and Commonwealth countries, but in the US the PMP is far more commonly requested. If you're targeting US roles, the PMP is usually the better choice.
